items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: Not long after I made my recording with Garnet Clarke, I met a fellow named Hugues Panassie and his friend Madeleine Gautier.

ctx.x: Garnet seemed to be a little deranged. When I recorded with him, I didn't know too much about him. Apparently, what had happened was that he had been down in the South of France, and all of a sudden he decided he wanted to come back to Paris. When he arrived there, he was going to stay at a certain hotel but he wanted first to see a lady friend of his. Unfortunately when they arrived, this lady was out, so he asked his taxi driver to drive around for a bit, but when they returned the lady was still not back. So…

Not long after I made my recording with Garnet Clarke, I met a fellow named Hugues Panassie and his friend Madeleine Gautier. I found out that Hugues was a jazz critic and president of the Hot Club de France. He knew

more about many of the American jazz musicians than I did and it was because of him that I was as well known as I was in France for my recording with Fats Waller. He had reviewed and written critics about the records before I knew that I was coming to France again.
